original_test_intent: Stress the specified BIOS ROM by programming and verifying the approved BIOS image exactly ten times with the physical SF600, then reinstall the same ROM in its SUT and prove normal power-on and BIOS boot.
original_method: A trained operator identifies and photographs the ROM, socket/header and orientation, captures a restorable baseline image and hash, validates the approved BIOS image, programmer, adapter, pinout and voltage, then performs ten separately logged program/readback/verify cycles. After safe disconnection and ROM reinstall, the operator powers on once and records BIOS identity and boot behavior.
manual_activity: A trained firmware operator attaches and operates the SF600, handles the ROM, performs the ten approved write/verify cycles, reinstalls it and observes physical power-on/BIOS boot. The owner authorizes destructive stress and decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board/ROM manufacturer, part, capacity, voltage, package, socket or header and orientation
Approved SF600 model, adapter/probe, vendor software/firmware version, pinout and programming profile
Signed approved BIOS image and immutable hash plus expected final BIOS identity
Baseline ROM dump/hash and tested recovery programmer, known-good image or spare ROM/board
Ten-cycle procedure, per-cycle acceptance, thermal/dwell limits, operator and explicit owner approval
Post-install power-on, BIOS screen/identity and boot acceptance plus isolation/quarantine plan
safety_requirements: De-energize and discharge the target per vendor procedure before attaching, removing or reinstalling ROM/programmer hardware
Verify target ROM, orientation, pinout and voltage independently before any erase or program action
Never substitute the reused-code release-note or fan-sensor variants for this destructive row
Stop at the first connection, current, temperature, erase, program, readback, verify or hardware anomaly and preserve the exact cycle evidence
Do not automatically retry, improvise a programmer profile, clear logs or continue toward ten after a failure
Disconnect the programmer and restore ROM/socket/board condition before SUT power-on

Review all ten cycle results plus final BIOS boot and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the vendor-approved SF600 software/profile at the physical station; capture its exact per-cycle program, readback and verify output. Any agent-side work is limited to read-only hashing and log reconciliation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SF600, BIOS code, exactly ten writes, ROM reinstall, SUT power-on/BIOS boot and the 5/0-minute source values remain unchanged.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL MANUAL TEN-CYCLE SF600 BIOS-ROM DURABILITY TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed destructive-test traveler binding ROM, programmer profile, image and operator, with baseline backup, ten numbered program/readback/verify bundles and a controlled reinstall/boot checkpoint.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds immutable identity, per-cycle evidence, stop conditions and independent recovery without replacing the ten-cycle stress.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final successful boot cannot prove every write verified, and ten successful programmer operations cannot prove the ROM was correctly reinstalled in the intended SUT; both evidence layers are required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong voltage, orientation, image or profile can irreversibly damage or corrupt the ROM/board; repeated writes may expose marginal behavior and must stop at the first fault.

project_override_considerations: A project may specify an in-circuit probe or socket adapter only through a versioned board/ROM procedure. Generic BMC-header wording cannot authorize connection, and fewer than ten successful cycles is incomplete source coverage.

SUT/board/ROM/socket-or-header identity, orientation, pinout/voltage, programmer/adapter/software/profile and operator
Approved BIOS image signature/hash, baseline ROM dump/hash, recovery-path proof and destructive-test approval
Ten numbered raw program/readback/verify logs with timestamps and hashes or the first preserved stop event
Safe disconnect/reinstall photos plus final ROM readback, SUT power-on, BIOS identity/screen and boot evidence
No-retry/no-log-clear audit, quarantine/recovery status and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master row consistently specifies an SF600 BIOS-ROM durability test and DeepSeek/GPT V2 agree on the physical boundary. DeepSeek's generic BMC-header phrase is treated as non-authoritative targeting detail, not as a contradiction in the preserved source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The source intent and exact ten-cycle method are reviewable. Physical programmer, target-specific instructions, image, approval and recovery are execution prerequisites, so the case is MANUAL ONLY rather than irreducibly blocked.

review_improvement: Binds destructive SF600 work to the correct reused-code variant, preserves the exact ten-write denominator and requires target, image, backup, per-cycle verification, reinstall and boot traceability.
independent_technical_reasoning: ROM durability is not established by a single final hash or final boot. Each destructive cycle must separately show successful programming and readback because a later write can mask an earlier failure. Conversely, programmer verification does not cover socket orientation, contact quality or platform boot compatibility after reinstall. Exact electrical targeting and an independent recovery path are mandatory before the first erase, and any failure terminates the sequence rather than triggering an automatic retry.
